# CANDIDATE: RECONCILIATION_LAYER_EVENTUALLY_CONSISTENT_READS

**Filed:** 2026-09-08  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** quality_gate  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Without a reconciliation layer for eventually-consistent reads in `conductor_outcome.py`, stale reads may cause false regression alarms by underreporting monotonic fields (e.g., trade counts, cumulative P&L). Implementing a layer that ensures monotonic fields are aggregated to the maximum across history prevents these false alarms while preserving true regression detection.

## Mechanism

In `conductor_outcome.py`, add a reconciliation step before reading eventually-consistent state: for each monotonic field (e.g., `total_trades`, `cumulative_pnl`), compare the read value with the last known good value from a local cache or write-ahead log, and take the maximum. This ensures fields never decrease due to replication lag. Add guard tests in `backtest/tests/test_conductor_outcome.py` that verify monotonic fields only increase or stay equal across sequential reads under simulated eventual consistency.
